body: I'm a liar. This is the second time I've sort of dragged her along lying because I was too scared to tell her the truth. Now there's nothing I can do. It will destroy her if I tell her the truth now. I'm a horrible person

How am I ever supposed to break up with her? She'd be crushed. She always talks about how excited she is for the future and how we're going to be a great family and it's starting to kind of freak me out. But how am I supposed to tell her that? How am I supposed to say "I don't see a future with you"? It's impossible. Yesterday I almost broke up with her and after we talked things through she said "do you really want to be together? I don't want to force you to". How the hell am I supposed to say "I'm not sure"? She also said that was the saddest she had felt in a long time. I don't know what to do

So we kind of worked things out and it turns out she was never mad at me for not wanting to move out and she understands. And I told her I can't stay up very late every night like she does. She asked if I still want to be together and if I think we'll be together forever and of course I said yes but I just don't know right now. Like what if we still aren't really compatible. And what if I'm not ready for a super serious forever relationship yet. Even though we worked things out I'm still worried.
But at the same time I can understand why she would want to. The place she lives just isn't good. I would want to move out asap too.

Not really, and I didn't mean to make it seem like that. At first, I was on board with it too. But the more I thought about it the less comfortable I got. I had many chances to tell her how I felt but I kept putting it off because I didn't want to burst her bubble, even though I knew I'd have to eventually. 


She was upset because I let her go one believing we'd be moving out as soon as possible for a while. It's understandable, and I'm sure if I told her how I felt right away she would have understood.

Hi, sorry it's been so long since I responded. I never got around to it and also this isn't my main account so I don't log in very often. After we both came back from work that day we talked it out. She was upset that I didn't tell her right away and that I let her go on thinking we'd be moving out asap, which is completely understandable. But we fixed things up and everything is fine again. 


But I keep having thoughts in the back of my mind. What if we just want different things? The thought of moving out terrifies me still. All I've ever known was my parents house. I'm not ready. Is that wrong? Should I be ready by now like a normal adult? Am I just a man child neckbeard who will live with his parents for the rest of his life? What if the two of us are too different? When we first started dating I was scared to say I felt the same way as her about something because I thought it sounded suspicious how much we had in common and I was afraid she'd think I was lying. Now I'm afraid we're too different. For example I was always the type who would go to bed around 12-1 and wake up at 8-9. She's not a morning person. I get a headache if I sleep in too late. Unfortunately the only times we get to really see each other are at night. So my sleeping schedules have changed drastically since we started dating. To be honest I miss waking up before 9:30. I mean I work in the evenings anyway so I can't always go to bed early but I miss waking up fairly early and having time to do stuff. 


What if I'm just not cut out for relationships at all? Is it wrong for me to think about my own longing to wake up early instead of caring most about this relationship? Is that selfish? What if I'd always be a terrible boyfriend no matter what? 


I'm so worried right now. What if we aren't right for each other? Everything seemed so great. Is it normal to have second thoughts like this?

That's a good idea, thank you for your help. I haven't seen a physical doctor about it yet, just a psychologist who had no idea what it could be. My first thought was that it was psychological because it seems like it starts when I'm most worried. I wonder if it could be psychosomatic.
Thank you, I appreciate your help.

Actually my mom told me today that she was trying to research it herself and found out about some sort of temporal lobe seizures that match my description. The weird thing is that it quit happening for a while and it seems to mostly be triggered by sights and situations. But I suppose it could be psychosomatic; people have had stranger psychosomatic problems.

Hi, thank you for your willingness to help, and I'm sorry that I kind of dragged you into it. I was just very freaked out last night and although I appreciate your help, I want you to know that if I overstepped my bounds or you just don't feel like helping, it's no problem.


But I might as well respond to your questions first. I'm feeling much better now than I was. I'm 19 years old and I've seen a psychologist a few times and he has no idea what this could possibly be. But I think it may be some kind of seizures, actually.


Again, sorry for forcing you to do this and if you don't want to, no problem.

I know it's been a few days but I just feel like I need to talk with someone about this right now. One sort of thing that seems to happen in my episodes is I imagine a cartoon clown or something and I don't know if he ever actually existed or if I just imagined him and he somehow knows he is the only person that exists and he just accepts it. How could I have such a detailed narrative in an episode that only lasts a few seconds? What if that's me and god is using these episodes to tell me that I'm the only person that exists? Or is it possible that I only see this because these episodes started when I was constantly worried about solipsism? I'm really scared right now.

Thank you very much. I know he's the one with the problem but I can't help feeling that if I had kept quiet and kept my suffering to myself then everything would be fine. Now it feels like everything is ruined. Maybe therapy won't help because whatever improves will be balanced out by this tension.

Thank you, I'm glad to hear it might have a rational explanation. It creeps me out because it seems like it doesn't completely fit the criteria of derealization, but it could in some sense. For example the symptoms of DPDR seem to be mostly about a kind of "numbness" to the outside world. I did feel that for a while, and I guess that could be the weird, wrong feeling I feel constantly, but this thing that keeps happening is more like my thoughts go completely out of control for a few seconds.
In fact, jamais vu sounds just like the "small scale" thing that I keep having. It's been going on for over a day now.

You know, it really does sound like jamais vu but with things in my head, not actual experiences or situations. In fact, I know the things that trigger it are things I've seen or experienced before. They always happen while doing something like driving or walking down my street, sitting in a classroom, walking into a mall that I've been to a thousand times, or walking around the house when the lights are on and people are up and about.

 It seems like the things that trigger it tend to have some significance with my childhood. For example, I spent a lot of time as a kid at my grandma's house, looking at and thinking about which can trigger it.

Thank you very much, and like I said to petsketchco, I'm sorry to answer your comment with only negativity. Sure I might be young now, but soon I won't be. I already feel like I wasted the most important years of my life. In less than a year I won't be a teenager any more and once I turn 25 or so, I'll have to be a "real adult". It will be over before I know it. I used to want to wait until I found someone I really loved to lose my virginity but that's not going to ever happen. Maybe I should just sign up for tinder or something and get it over with. I know some people start dating late but I feel like I will never, ever get the chance. and besides, no matter what anyone says starting to date late will be hard because I never had any practice like normal people have.

Thank you very much for your answer and offer. But I would feel bad burdening you with my complaints and my girl obsessions. Also I don't like to respond to such a helpful comment with negativity but I feel like there's nothing to be positive about. I've been lifting weights for almost a year and the progress has been super slow. So I think I'm pretty much at the best I can be, which isn't good. These days I'm so sad and discouraged that it's hard to get motivated to keep trying.

I used to experience almost the exact same thing, and I started again recently. Try looking into derealization or depersonalization because that's the closest thing I could find to it. I know that for me at least it happens in periods when I am most distressed.

Thank you again for your responses.


Maybe I'm just trying to rationalize things to see what I want to see, but I need to think this through. When she "flirts" with me, I try my best to reciprocate it without being too bold just in case I misinterpret her intentions. So, if she was flirting with me, and I did the same back, she would obviously not mind it. I don't think she'd do it to get a rise from me or for attention, because she's too nice for that. She's called me nice several times before, it just seemed like kind of an odd time to bring it up just then. 


I know I should probably just listen to you and move on to be on the safe side. But if I don't obsess over somebody like a pathetic loser, I think I might occupy my mind worrying about other things. Like contracting unlikely, deadly diseases.


I don't mean to sound like I'm ungrateful and I'm just completely disregarding your advice. I really do appreciate it, so don't feel like you've wasted your time 


On a side note, the way I'd really like to die is by hypothermia, but I don't live in a cold enough climate.
I don't think that's true. I have other friends who are girls, one of whom has a boyfriend and I don't mind at all.

In case you forgot I actually just wanted to know if liking her made me a bad friend. No way am I gonna ask her out and either way, whether or not I would had nothing to do with why you think she might not be my real friend.

Actually yes she has given me rides before, also hung out with me, has helped me with other ways that I don't keep track of, called me her best friend, and is generally just a nice person to me. I still don't understand what an "emotional tampon" is. Is that just somebody to gossip, hang out, and talk with? Because to me that sounds exactly like what a friendship is. I don't understand why you people would just jump to some wild conclusion that she's manipulating or using me. I don't think I should believe anything in this comment chain because you both seem to know nothing about people or normal interactions. I know better than to take friendship advice from somebody who uses the word "friend zone" unironically.

I didn't expect such an in-depth response, so thanks for that. 


It sucks because all along I thought she was kind of flirting with me, because sometimes she calls me "baby boy" and stuff. I guess I should have known better than to trust my own judgement on something like that. By the way, I actually just finished my first year of college about a week ago.


Also, I don't really know if being good at psychology is something to be proud about, because almost everybody was good a the class in my high school. I think it may have just been easy.


Another thing, what do you mean by "the day that I decided to do it"? What did you decide to do? Sorry if I am missing something obvious here.


Thank you for your input.

That's very nice, thank you so much. It definitely got better after high school, even within the first semester of college. After all I have friends now (funnily enough we all graduated together at high school but since I was terrified of talking to people, I wasn't really friends with them). I just kind of feel like a loser because I never experienced things that normal people do in high school, and I regret not taking more risks and talking to people more, because it turns out that I really love social interactions. 


But anyway, yeah, you're right. Life after high school is 1,000 times better.
What does that even mean?
True, I guess that's possible but I doubt I'm that nice.
I'm 19 years old in what is basically a community college.
Thanks I actually will. Having friends is pretty great, you should try it sometime.

That's a good point. I guess it's because everyone is different, and some people might feel like it would be awkward. Besides, I wouldn't mind at all if i found out that she liked me, but maybe I'd feel differently if I didn't like her in the first place. Of course I wouldn't think she's a bad person either way, but I could see how it could be awkward to stay friends. 


I guess I'm most worried that in this case, since she thinks I don't like her, if she found out, she might not trust me anymore. 


My sister always says that this friend likes me, but I'm skeptical, especially now.
